test_title: PYST 5: SSC JE EE - General Awareness (Held On 10 Oct 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: During which census enumeration did the Registrar General of India provide for the first time three codes for enumeration i.e., Male-1, Female-2 and Others-3?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2011**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Registrar General of India introduced three enumeration codes for gender in the **2011 **Census of India: **Male-1, Female-2, and Others-3.**
 
• This was a significant change from previous censuses, which had only two codes for gender: Male and Female.
 
• The introduction of the Others code was intended to be** more inclusive **of people** who do not identify with the traditional binary gender categories of Male and Female.**
 
• The Others code was used to **enumerate people who identified as transgender, genderqueer, or any other gender identity that is not Male or Female.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian census of 2011 was the** 15th National census **of India since 1872 and was conducted in two phases: the House-listing (Housing Census) from April 2010 to September 2010 and the Population Enumeration during February 2011.
 
• The significant feature of this census was that, for the first time, it included "**Others**" as a gender category, apart from Male and Female.
 
• The 2011 census revealed that there were** approx 487,000** individuals who identified themselves as** 'Others'**, thereby bringing the third gender into the validation of the official statistic report.
